text: My birds whisper that Gandalf (1) and Hermione (2) seem to have been lingering near one another’s stalls more than most this morning, and likewise Yoda (3) and Batman (4) have been seen sharing a pot of spiced tea near the eastern brazier. It’s the sort of thing that catches the eye when the bazaar is still finding its rhythm — though of course, birds can mis-see as easily as they can see.

My birds say Gandalf (1), your ledger line was a lantern held too steady — the clean page cannot reveal who shuttered what, only who claims to read it. And Hermione (2), your voice may carry far, but Yoda (3), when your lantern swings too close to the dark corners, even the dimmest truth casts a shadow — did you truly see shuttered stalls, or only the fear of seeing one?

Elsa (7): My birds say Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, but steady looms do not always weave the cloth they claim—who taught you to spin so smooth a thread? And Gandalf (1), an empty ledger is a ledger that cannot read itself, yet the bazaar trades in ledgers that *do* read back. Sherlock (10), shadows cling longest to those who measure them longest—did you step into the dark yourself last night, or only count the steps from a safe distance?

Yoda (3), your lantern swings bright, but braziers light the stall, not the ledger—when the loom is empty, the light only shows the empty pockets. Ripley (5), spice and iron may scent the air, but the bazaar’s true perfume is the ledger’s ink—what name did it write at midnight if no one was looking?

Neo (6), silence is a loom without thread, but looms do not weave silence—they wait for hands to pull the shuttle. Morpheus (8), your kiln waits for metal, yet the bazaar’s fire is cold this morning; who banked the coals?
